long_biography.plain_text:
For William Ramonas, protecting a company's most valuable buildings required engineers to examine the buildings themselves. At Global Risk Consultants, he challenged the growing reliance on computer catastrophe models when detailed structural knowledge was needed. The firm's partnership with Miyamoto International brought structural engineers into assessments of hurricane, windstorm and flood exposure.

His concern was practical: a model suitable for an insurer's vast portfolio could be poorly suited to safeguarding an individual company's critical sites. Reflecting on Hurricane Andrew, he explained why distance from the coast was no longer enough. Assessors needed to understand local wind forces and a building's ability to withstand them.
